title: One GRPO step on a bandit
goal:
Take a policy with no state: a softmax over $K$ arms with logits `logits`, where an "output" is one arm. A group is $G$ pulls with rewards `rewards`. The paper does one update after each exploration stage (Section 4.2), so $\pi_{\theta_{old}} = \pi_\theta$, the ratio is 1, and the clip is inactive. The gradient of Equation 3 is then the coefficient of Equation 20 times $\nabla_\theta\log\pi_\theta(a_i)$:

$$\frac1G\sum_{i=1}^G\Big(\hat A_i + \beta\Big(\frac{\pi_{ref}(a_i)}{\pi_\theta(a_i)} - 1\Big)\Big)\,\nabla_\theta\log\pi_\theta(a_i)$$

Write `grpo_update(logits, actions, rewards, logits_ref, lr, beta)`. It returns `logits + lr * gradient` and doesn't change its inputs. The starter gives you `softmax` and a finished `group_advantages`. For a softmax policy, $\nabla_{\text{logits}}\log\pi(a) = \mathrm{onehot}(a) - \pi$.
hints: `pi = softmax(logits)` and `pi_ref = softmax(logits_ref)`. The KL coefficient uses `pi_ref[actions] / pi[actions]`, with the reference on top.
Build `coef = adv + beta * (pi_ref[actions] / pi[actions] - 1)`, a vector of length `G`. Then `grad = (coef[:, None] * (np.eye(K)[actions] - pi)).mean(axis=0)`.
The advantages sum to 0, but the KL part of the coefficient doesn't, so the `- pi` term matters once `beta > 0`. The tests check the gradient against finite differences of the objective.
Return a new array. Don't write into `logits`.
